targets.authors: Savani, K., Markus, H. R., Naidu, N. V. R., Kumar, S., & Berlia, N.
targets.title: What counts as a choice? US Americans are more likely than Indians to construe actions as choices.
targets.evidence_quote: We selected the study 3 claim that Americans tend to construe more of another actor’s actions as choices than do Indian participants; Americans therefore identify more instances in a video as times when the actor made a choice. This reflects the following statement from the paper's abstract: "[W]e found that people in U.S. American contexts, where the disjoint model of agency is prevalent, are more likely than those in Indian contexts to construe … other individuals’ behaviors as choices" This claim was tested in Study 3 by submitting the number of button presses made by participants in either a control condition (pressing a button every time the actor touches an object with his hands) or the construal-of-choice condition (pressing a bottom whenever the actor made a choice) to a 2 (culture) × 2 (condition) ANOVA. This analysis yielded an interaction between culture (Indian, American) and condition (construal-of-choice vs. control task) in how often participants pressed the response button, F(1, 120) = 5.69, p < .02, p_rep = .96
targets.outcome_computational_quote: The reproduction attempt was mostly successful. an interaction between culture (Indian, American) and condition (construal-of-choice vs. control task) in how often participants pressed the response button, F(1, 123) = 6.12, p = 0.0147.

targets.outcome_reasoning: Comparable ANOVA output was produced, but the reported F and denominator degrees of freedom differ (6.12 and 123 versus 5.69 and 120). The report calls the attempt mostly successful rather than exact recovery. Only push-button recovery is reported; no alternative specification robustness test.
